SNPs in HSPA1 genes are associated with risk and disease severity of COPD secondary to tobacco smoking, and differences in the intracellular levels of Hsp are found depending on the source of the exposure to smoke.
SNPs in HSPA1 are associated with risk to COPD and severity of the disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of HSP SNPs in COPD secondary to tobacco smoking and biomass-burning smoke.

the role of genetic variation in HSP genes in COPD susceptibility and severity, as well as with the effect of biomass-burning smoke and tobacco smoking exposure on mRNA and intracellular protein levels.

the identification of genetic factors that could contribute to COPD risk in smokers, as well as in those exposed to biomass burning smoke, which could help to identify individuals at risk for developing the disease and to establish personalized treatment strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HSP gene SNPs, as well as mRNA and Hsp levels, are associated with the development of COPD secondary to tobacco smoking and exposure to biomass-burning pollution.
HSPs and their SNPs are involved in COPD development, but further studies are needed to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.
the SNPs in HSPA1 genes are associated with COPD risk, severity, and exposure source.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HSP genes are involved in the pathogenesis of COPD and the risk of developing this disease is influenced by SNPs and the exposition source.

SNPs in HSPA1 genes are associated with an increased susceptibility of smokers and those chronically exposed to smoke from biomass burning to COPD, and that the levels of Hsp27 and other HSP family members could be used as biomarkers for the diagnosis of COPD.
the HSPA1A gene is a potential biomarker of COPD related to biomass burning smoke.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SNPs in HSPA1 genes could be used as biomarkers to predict the risk of developing COPD, as well as for the severity of the disease.
SNPs in HSPA1 genes may play an important role in the development of COPD, which is related to the exposure source.
HSP genes could be considered as a biomarker for the susceptibility of COPD development and severity, depending on the exposition to tobacco smoking and/or biomass burning smoke.
